metadata.title: Pick a Line — Extending walker-jumpman
metadata.note: Walker-mode godot-waikthrough of walker-jumpman-bao-x. Gameplay beats B02-B06 are REAL engine capture at native 3840x2160, scripted input, labeled on screen; holds are labeled HELD FRAME. The only human playtest is recorded in the game's TEST-REPORT.md section 7 and is explicitly NOT claimed as evidence of discoverability, because the player designed the level. B00's prompt is an illustrative reconstruction, labeled as such. No upload.

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 1 — ClaudeComposerAsk. Prompt is an ILLUSTRATIVE RECONSTRUCTION, labeled on screen; it is not a historical transcript. No fabricated build receipts.
beats.narration_text: Annyeong — this is Liam, in for Bear. Bao Xing took Nik Bear Brown's walker-jumpman, a small Godot platformer with two gaps and a spike, and was asked to give it a new character and a new section. Here is the kind of ask that starts that work. This prompt is a reconstruction for the film, not a recording of the original session.

show.event: composer card fades in on cream
'ILLUSTRATIVE RECONSTRUCTION' badge sets above the composer

prompt types: 'Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a small readable 2D platformer — one fixed-height jump, unlimited retries — into a playable Godot project, then extend it with a new character and a new section that asks the player to choose a route.'
send button arms terracotta

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a small, readable 2D platformer — one fixed-height jump, forgiving input windows, unlimited retries — into a playable Godot project. Then extend it: a new main character, and a new section that makes the player choose a route instead of just surviving one.
props.runningText: reconstructing the ask — not a transcript of the original session…
output: Starter: two gaps, a spike, a flag.
Added: a courier, and a fork.

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 2 — what was ACTUALLY built. Hesitant-writer correction: 'a new game' struck to 'an extension'. States the slice's real limits.
beats.narration_text: What exists is not a new game. It is the starter, unmodified below x nine hundred and sixty, plus two additions: a character called the Lamp-Head Courier, and a section called Pick a Line. Forty-nine automated checks pass, twenty-five of them the starter's own, unaltered. Cherries, audio, settings and an export are still not built, and this film will not pretend otherwise.

beats.role_note: CAUSE AND EFFECT 1 — the required source-change-to-behaviour link. Two numbers from the starter's own tuning decide the whole trap. FRAMEWORK beat.
beats.narration_text: That trap is not a timer and not a random event. It is two numbers from the starter's tuning, untouched. Standing, the player's collider occupies y two ninety-two to three twenty. At the top of a jump it occupies two thirty-six to two sixty-four. Those two bands do not overlap. So an arming rectangle placed between them, at two forty-four to two eighty-four, is provably unreachable on foot and provably reachable in the air. Walking can never spring it. Leaving the ground always will.

beats.role_note: CAUSE AND EFFECT 2 — the probe rejecting the first level design. Source-backed: real probe output. Honest about the design being wrong first.
beats.narration_text: The same arithmetic killed Bao's first level. The plan stacked the two roads, with spikes under the ledges. A reachability probe swept real takeoff positions through real physics and returned: unreachable, unreachable, blocked. A jumping head reaches two thirty-six; the ledges sat at two seventy-two. You cannot jump under them. The fix was geometry, not a bigger jump — and a check named tuning-unchanged proves the jump was never touched.

beats.role_note: VERDICT LAW — observed vs untested vs next. Names the revision and the human/AI split. Must not overclaim the single playtest.
beats.narration_text: Verdict. Observed working: both routes reach the relocated finish, the trap punishes the jump and spares the walk, the coin is reachable only from the high line, and forty-nine checks pass with the starter's twenty-five unaltered. Untested: the only human playtest was by the person who designed the level, so discoverability for a stranger is unknown. And the high road still costs the same six hundred and seventy-one ticks as the low road — it pays in a coin, not in time. Next improvement: put it in front of someone who has never seen it, and watch where they stop.

beats.role_note: YOUR TURN LAW — a runnable Walker prompt relevant to THIS video, read in full, then one concrete experiment. Liam signs off here.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. If you are extending someone else's level, paste this before you commit to a layout: 'Read this project's tuning values, then write a throwaway script that sweeps real takeoff positions through the real physics and tells me which of my planned jumps actually land. Do not change the jump to make my layout work.' Bao's probe rejected a design he had already hand-computed and believed. The moment you reach for jump strength, you have stopped extending the game and started editing it to agree with you. Liam, in for Bear.
